newsitem.title: USA: BRC Holdings to sell election unit.
newsitem.headline: BRC Holdings to sell election unit.

text.p: BRC Holdings Inc said Friday it agreed to sell its election business to American Information Systems Inc for $59.3 million.
BRC said it expects to record a pre-tax gain of about $30 million or more on the deal.

"This divestiture will enable us to concentrate on growing our data processing and information products businesses," said P.E. Esping, BRC's chairman. "We will now focus our activities on serving our customers through our government services, health care and consulting divisions."
Under terms of the deal, American Information will pay $35 million in cash, $17.5 million in a subordinated note and 19.9 percent of the equity of American Information.

The final closing of the deal is subject to review by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and adjustment of the purchase price based on changes in the net book value of the election business through the date of closing, American Information said.
To the election unit divestiture, BRC said it may have to recharacterize its merger with Pace Group Inc as a "purchase" for accounting purposes, rather than a "pooling of interests."
Such a re-characterization would result in about $10.4 million of increased intangible assets and certain corresponding increases in amortization expenses connected with the Pace deal, BRC said.
BRC's merger with Pace was consummated on Sept. 5, 1996.
